newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel cancels monetary tender.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel cancels monetary tender.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Wednesday it had cancelled its daily monetary tender to commercial banks because of surplus liquidity.

The surplus liquidity is the result of market intervention by the central bank, which has bought foreign currency to prevent the shekel from appreciating beyond the band in which it is allowed to trade, the central bank said.
The tender is for daily loans to commercial banks. The central bank did not say if the tender would be renewed on Thursday.
Dealers said the central bank had intervened in trading on Wednesday.

The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies on Tuesday and Wednesday following a sharp decline on Monday, triggered by the political unrest between Israel and the Palestinians.
The central bank cancelled a number of its monetary tenders in the past two months because of surplus liquidity caused by high government spending as well as central bank interventions.
In July the central bank's weekly tenders to commercial banks were halted.
